ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=70^\circ$, and $\odot O$ is the inscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$. What is the value of $\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\odot O$ is the inscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$,

it follows that OB bisects $\angle ABC$, and OC bisects $\angle ACB$,

therefore, $\angle OBC = \frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$, and $\angle OCB = \frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$,

hence, $\angle OBC + \angle OCB = \frac{1}{2}(\angle ABC + \angle ACB) = \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - \angle A)$,

thus, $\angle BOC = 180^\circ - (\angle OBC + \angle OCB) = 180^\circ - \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ - \angle A) = 90^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\angle A = 90^\circ + \frac{1}{2} \times 70^\circ = \boxed{125^\circ}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Since $\odot O$ is the inscribed circle of $\triangle ABC$, OB bisects $\angle ABC$ and OC bisects $\angle ACB$. So $\angle OBC = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle ABC$ and $\angle OCB = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle ACB$. Then $\angle OBC + \angle OCB = \tfrac{1}{2}(\angle ABC + \angle ACB) = \tfrac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle A)$. Hence $\angle BOC = 180^\circ-(\angle OBC+\angle OCB)=180^\circ-\tfrac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle A)=90^\circ+\tfrac{1}{2}\angle A=90^\circ+\tfrac{1}{2}\times70^\circ=\boxed{125^\circ}$.

Then reason: Because ⊙O is the incircle of △ABC, O is the incenter of the triangle, OB bisects ∠ABC, and OC bisects ∠ACB. Therefore ∠OBC = ∠B/2, ∠OCB = ∠C/2. In △ABC, ∠A = 70°, so ∠B + ∠C = 180° - 70° = 110°. Thus ∠OBC + ∠OCB = (∠B + ∠C)/2 = 110°/2 = 55°. In △BOC, ∠BOC = 180° - 55° = 125°.
